pos.personaBrief: Dortmund 2011-13 won the ball and went forward at once (BR: counterattack, ball forward immediately; Cox: defending deep suited their counters), not seeking possession for its own sake.

pro.personaBrief: BVB played the ball forward immediately and sprinted into space (BR), with a direct, quick counter style (Hard Tackle) and 'purely one-dimensional' play that wasted little time in possession.

est.personaBrief: Wide midfielders tucked inside (Cox), Hummels dribbled into midfield and the 4-2-3-1 flexed to 4-2-4 or 4-4-1-1, so roles were fluid and close together around counter-pressing, though not a pure relational school.

lar.personaBrief: Wide midfielders tucked inside (Cox) while Piszczek ran the byline, so attacks were fast and central via the 10 (Kagawa/Reus) with full-back width.

blo.personaBrief: Counter-pressing was the core (FFT: counter-pressing gets us to goal quicker; Klopp: best playmaker) with a high line; BR says they struggle to defend deep, though Cox notes a medium block.

mar.personaBrief: Counter-pressing was space-oriented (VOOR) and organised in a medium block, with no evidence of dedicated man-marking; set pieces not found, so zonal default.

pla.personaBrief: Klopp: 'Real Madrid will not make us change our style'; BVB kept one model, though Hard Tackle and BR show small adjustments (Bender vs Kehl by opponent).

res.personaBrief: Klopp said games that become boring lose their right to exist and BVB played at breakneck, entertaining pace, with all-out attack even at risk.

sis.personaBrief: The team was not built around one player (Hard Tackle), ordinary players like Piszczek were transformed into stars by the system (BR), and everyone worked in the counter-press.

jog.personaBrief: Breakneck pace and heavy running (BR, Cox 118km anecdote) demand intensity and speed, but Gundogan-type passers were valued in midfield and Hummels built up.

bas.personaBrief: Dortmund had an average age near 23, youth development and a modest wage scale (BR, Hard Tackle, Watzke 'young players extend credit'), though Kehl stayed as an icon.

lid.personaBrief: Football Espana describes a teacher-student relationship with unquestioning authority; the team was not built around any star, with Klopp setting uniform demands.
